newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks sharply lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks sharply lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fell sharply in early Thursday morning with the blue chip Hang Seng Index slipping 150 points, or 1.02 percent, to 14,553 in quiet trading.

"The market opened weak on the recent negative sentiment and the steep fall on Wall Street last night," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "But it seems there is good support close to the 14,500 level (on the Hang Seng Index)."
The Dow industrial closed 119.88 points lower at 7,842.43 on Wednesday.
Brokers said early losses were trimmed after bargain hunters moved in at lower levels.
The Hang Seng stood at 14,641, down 62 points, after the first 25 minutes of trade. The red chip index rebounded from an early 72-point loss to trade three points down at 3,073.
"Some small retail investor jumped in snapping up red chips which triggered a technical rebound on the red chip index," said Dennis Leung, research manager at J & A Securities.
Ng Fung Hong rose HK$0.25 to HK$10.30, China Resources was up HK$0.70 to HK$32.30 and Shanghai Industrial added HK$0.40 at HK$45.40.
But brokers said red chips should continue to consolidate in the short term after the rebound.
Among blue chips, property counters recovered from their recent fall with the sectoral Hang Seng sub-index gaining 92 points, or 0.39 percent, to 23,925.
Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$0.75 to HK$87.50 and Hednerson Land added HK$0.50 to HK$66.00 but Cheung Kong eased HK$0.50 at HK$74.25.
Leung said he expected the Hang Seng Index to stay in a consolidation mode, moving between 14,600 and 14,800 for the rest of the day.
July index futures eased 85 points to 14,640 in early trade.
